sets.title: Authorization decision: state machine vs scattered concerns expression
sets.description: The same resource-authorization decision in three semantically equivalent forms: carrier A uses the pristine guard-clause boolean-return form, carrier B uses a finite state machine with explicit state transitions UNKNOWN→USER_VALID→ROLE_CHECKED→OWNER_CHECKED→GRANT_CHECKED→ALLOWED/DENIED (sem_state_machine variant), and carrier C expresses authorization with scattered-concerns variable naming indicating different logical classes (sem_scatter variant). All three compute behaviorally identical results. No two carriers share a token run long enough for token/line tools to pair them, so only semantic detection is expected to recover the cluster.
sets.notes: SEM-09 variant (sem_state_machine) uses explicit state machine transitions. SEM-08 variant (sem_scatter) uses scattered-concerns variable naming. Behavioral equivalence enforced by gen/seeds/access_guard/equivalence_test.php.

distractors.reason: near-miss: same auth vocabulary (user/resource/roles/grants/status) but computes a numeric trust score, not a boolean decision
